creator: syntaix.ai
caption:
💬 Comment "REMIND" and I'll send you the GitHub repo. 👇

Someone just open-sourced REMIND—an AI vision system that helps robots remember objects even after they disappear from view.
Unlike traditional object trackers that rely on motion or position, REMIND builds a long-term visual memory using advanced AI vision models.

Here's what makes it different:
🧠 Remembers objects after they leave the camera's view
👀 Uses DINOv3 visual features to recognize the same object from different angles
🧩 Understands object parts instead of treating every object as a single image
📍 Uses surrounding objects as context to improve identification accuracy
🔄 Continuously updates its memory as the environment changes
⚠️ Can even detect when it's uncertain instead of making incorrect identity predictions

This could be a huge step forward for:
🤖 Autonomous robots
📦 Warehouse automation
🏠 Home assistant robots
🚗 Indoor navigation systems
👁️ Computer vision research

Instead of simply tracking movement, REMIND focuses on remembering visual identity, making long-term object tracking much more reliable in real-world environments.

⭐ It's fully open source, so developers can study it, build on it, or integrate it into their own robotics and computer vision projects.

This AI skill lets you scrape platforms like Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, and Chinese platforms like XiaoHongShu and Bilibili.

It's a free open source CLI tool built for Claude Code, Cursor, and other AI agents.

Now it's one command and a few minutes of login.

caption:
Comment "API" to get this free GitHub repo with over 25+ Free AI API Key Providers. 

You don't need to pay for AI API keys anymore.

Instead, use this free GitHub repo called free-llm-api-resources, and it lists down every free API provider out there.

It gives you free access to top models like Kimi, DeepSeek, Gemini, and more, all for completely free.

You just pick a provider like OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM, or Google AI Studio, generate your API key.

Then plug it straight into Claude Code, Cursor, or whatever you're working on.

Some providers give you more room than others though. 

OpenRouter gives you up to 1,000 requests a day once you add a small lifetime top-up.

NVIDIA NIM gives you 40 requests a minute with just phone verification.

Google AI Studio is another solid one, since it gives you access to Gemini models with generous daily limits, and it doesn't require any payment info at all to get started.

There's also a second list in the repo for providers that hand out trial credits instead of fully free access. 

Fireworks, Nebius, and Hyperbolic all give you a small credit balance to test bigger models before committing to anything.

So if you're building an agent that calls a model constantly, or you just want to try five different providers before picking a favorite, this repo saves you the trouble of hunting each one down individually.

Perfect for AI agents, side projects, or just testing things out without spending a dollar.

You can now run Claude Code for completely free, with almost unlimited usage.

Someone on GitHub just built a free tool called OmniRoute.

It links your Claude Code to over 200 free AI providers.

The moment your Claude limit runs out, it automatically switches you to the next best model.

So your session keeps going without any interruption.

Think of it like a relay race.

When one runner gets tired, the next one picks up the baton without breaking stride.

Plus it compresses your prompts before they even reach the model.

This cuts your token usage by up to 90%, while keeping the same output quality.

That's the part most routing tools get wrong. They save you money on rate limits but still burn through tokens fast.

OmniRoute attacks both problems at once.

It works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, and basically every AI coding tool out there.

One config file, and your entire setup runs on free models.

Setup takes minutes. Just one npm install, and you're routing through 200+ providers instantly.

For developers tired of hitting daily limits mid-project, this changes how much you can actually build in a day.

creator: heystevetan
caption:
I’ve found the single biggest time saver for any founder doing outreach this year.

So these Italian developers released a free open source AI tool on Github that already has 28000 stars and I’ll tell you why. 

ScrapeGraph has an MCP server that connects straight into Claude. Once it's set up, you can hand Claude any research job you want. 

Something like, go scrape competitor product pages across Amazon and Shopify, pull every product name, price, review count, and rating, and drop it into a sheet. Instant market research on what's actually selling. Claude runs the whole job in the background and hands you a clean list at the end.

And it isn’t just Amazon, you can scrape information from any website like glassdoor reviews, x accounts, email addresses and much more. 

Here's the best part. There are actually two ways to run this. If you're comfortable with a bit of setup, ScrapeGraph is fully open source on GitHub. You can plug in your own API keys and run it completely free forever. 

If you'd rather skip the setup, there's a hosted version that starts at around 17 dollars a month, which still undercuts tools like Apify and Bright Data that used to charge 50 to 500 dollars for the same job.

For any founder trying to find the right people to talk to, this is one of the fastest ways to skip the grunt work and get straight to the conversations that actually grow your business.
